speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether he can provide an update on the Government's study on sodium taxes in countries where such measures have been implemented; (b) when will recommendations on potential policy changes arising from this study be put out; and (c) how does the Government intend to ensure that efforts to address sodium overconsumption do not inadvertently lead to increased business overhead costs and higher food prices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We need to cut down on our consumption of sodium urgently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Other countries have faced similar challenges and the Ministry of Health (MOH) has studied what they have done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Chile has implemented regulations in 2016 to require food and drinks high in sugar, salt and saturated fat to have a warning label.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: You can find such warning labels on soft drinks, sauces, processed meats and so on, in Chile.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Finland has also successfully used food labelling laws to reduce salt consumption over the past three decades.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, our Nutri-grade labelling measures for pre-packaged beverages has been very effective in bringing down sugar consumption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We should likewise tackle excessive sodium consumption in a way that is suited to our context.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In many European and Western countries, their main source of sodium is processed foods which households buy from shops or supermarkets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In Singapore, sodium comes mainly from added salt, sauces and seasonings, such as soya sauce, dark sauce, fish sauce and chili sauce, and we consume them most when we eat out.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: A key priority is therefore to work with the manufacturers of salt and sauces.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As a result, lower-sodium alternatives are now more accessible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The other stakeholder to engage are food operators such as hawkers, restaurants, caterers and chefs to promote the adoption of lower-sodium ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We will have to explain to them the need to cut our sodium intake, introduce them to lower-sodium ingredients, as well as provide them with samples that they can try out so that we can get them to use these products.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We also hope that they will help us explain to the public that salt is an acquired taste and that if we over-consume it over some time, our taste buds will get accustomed to it and fail to taste other natural ingredients.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: We are planning a series of engagement sessions with them, including with the industry and professional associations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: In Singapore, less salt often means more taste as it allows us to appreciate the natural flavours of the herbs, spices and other ingredients typically used in local cuisine.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: HPB will continue to educate Singaporeans on the need to cut sodium, increase their receptiveness to using lower-sodium ingredients and change the perception that we need more salt and sauces for flavourful dishes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It will conduct more activities, such as food sampling activities at supermarkets.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: I mean, after all the efforts that you have done, does HPB know what is the number of households that have switched over to potassium salt?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: And on the impact on businesses, she mentioned a grant was given for the food processing businesses for them to use potassium salt for their products.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: How much grant has been issued and what are the plans to promote this scheme further, including to the households as well?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I do not have the specific numbers and the data that the Member has requested.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But if he so wishes, he can file another Parliamentary Question and I can provide information.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I want to explain that we are cognisant of the concerns of consumers, especially in relation to the cost, as we move to the lower -sodium products.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And we actually take a multi-pronged approach and an upstream approach in this to ensure that various stakeholders are with us and therefore will help alleviate the issues of cost.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, if there is anything to go by, these are healthy numbers which show growing appreciation and support for these efforts, and HPB has also garnered the commitment of major manufacturers and leaders in the food service sector to reduce sodium in their products and their food.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this I think is something that we are going to continue to build on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The third prong of this effort is, of course, our public education and that is important because it is not just the upstream and the supply but also public.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, there is going to be efforts that we are going to be complementing.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I mentioned earlier, there are going to be campaigns.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There has been actually a campaign, and this is a multi-year public education campaign to raise awareness of the effects of high sodium intake, educate public on the available lower-sodium alternatives and ways to actually replace salt totally without compromising on taste.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, we are looking at a multi-pronged upstream effort, which we hope will then change the ecosystem and have everybody on board in this effort.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: As a follow-up question – will the food labelling of low-sodium food products and sauces be made mandatory?

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak
text: Or the other way around: will high-sodium food warning signs and labels be made mandatory?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It will probably come in phases because, as the Member knows, we need to prepare the operators and the providers as well.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, this is something that we will announce as we roll it out and hopefully, we bring the whole community with us on this.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: Just one supplementary question based on the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's answer.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to check, the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned this grant that is made available to producers to introduce alternatives or manufacturing processes to lower the sodium input into the products and the food that eventually comes out.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I am just wondering what is the uptake rate of this scheme?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: How many producers have actually been granted and what is the size of the average grants, and what are the efforts to be made to encourage more producers to take up this grant in order to reformulate some of the manufacturing processes?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: As I explained to Dr Lim earlier, I do not have the specific numbers and data here and I will be happy to answer the question if the Member files an additional question.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But earlier, I also alluded to the different numbers and the different parties that we have been working with and the uptake on that front.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I think this is all hands on deck and a multi-pronged approach, upstream approach on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: If we do work with the suppliers, the costs then need not be transferred to the hawkers, to the restaurants, all consumers will also not be affected.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I hope that something is that we can get Members to also continue to share and encourage – these are different groups that we are talking about.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are working upstream, but at the same time, we also need the community to avail themselves to some of these products.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Because as you know, when there is a higher demand for healthier food, for low-sodium options, this will also encourage the food service providers to move towards this direction.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, I hope that there will be a whole-of-community support in this effort.
